Commentary.Commentary: With that, the ODI series comes to an end and we will now move to the 2-match T20I series. The first match will be on Tuesday, 6th of September. It will begin on 1900 IST in the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium. Until then, it is a warm good bye from us, take care and see you soon.

MAN OF THE SERIES - GEORGE BAILEY for his outstanding batting wins the award. He says it has been a challenging series and it was tough to adapt to the conditions. Says the partnership with Warner was very satisfying and says they had to come with different plans after the Test series. Also said they practiced a few different shots and feels it came to good use. Feels that the hardest thing is getting starts but once you take your time you can be really good as Warner showed tonight.

DINESH CHANDIMAL says that they were very disappointing with the bat and says they haven't been able to reach the 260-270 mark. Says they have experienced players and good youngsters and wants them to learn from the mistakes and come back stronger next time. On his captaincy role, he says he is enjoying it for sure.

MAN OF THE MATCH - DAVID WARNER says thanks on receiving the award but gives credit to the boys for overcoming the new ball. Further says that the partnership was key in the game and appreciates Bailey's efforts throughout the series, calling him 'the rock' of the team. On losing the the toss but winning the match says it is a tough call to make whether it will be a Heads or Tails but says his team did well to take the wickets regularly.

Sri Lanka are a young side with tremendous potential, only time will tell whether they can really make it count for something big. For now, it is congratulations to Australia on the winning the series 4-1.

For Sri Lanka, only Perera and de Silva were amongst the wickets. The former took the early wickets of Wade and Khawaja to put Sri Lanka in a commanding position. However, a lack of contribution from other bowlers never really caused trouble for the visitors. The Lankans need to really take a good look at their performance in this series and make sure that their mistakes are not repeated in the future.

Bailey gave good support but he departed right before his half-century but with Warner in the middle, the game was still in Australia's favor. Though Warner could not stay till the end, his contribution was enough to put Australia in a winning position. In the end, the visitors got past the finish line.

However, Warner and Bailey stuck and ensured they did not throw their wickets away. The two took no risk initially and only focused on rotating the strike and taking singles every now and then. Warner played himself into form and became the first Australian to score a ton in Sir Lanka.

After a dismal Test performance, Australia have come roaring back into the ODI series. The run chase always looked easy for the Aussies but Wade and Khawaja gave an early scare to the visitors. With Finch injured and Warner looking out of touch, the early wickets of the duo piled pressure and gave Sri Lanka a sniff at the game.

Welcome back for the run chase! 196 is what the Aussies need to win 4-1, will they be able to do so? They have to bat with a positive intent if they are to chase this down. For now, we are happy that the rain gods have showed mercy and let's hope for it to stay this way for the second half. Out come the players and the umpires. Finch won't be opening as he met with an injury earlier. DAVID WARNER and MATTHEW WADE to open for the Aussies. SURANGA LAKMAL to have a go with the ball with a slip in place. Let's play...
